key_insight: A two-stage "Mine and Refine" contrastive framework that first harvests scalable weak supervision and then refines embeddings to explicitly model graded relevance (exact match, substitutes, complements), improving multi-category e‑commerce retrieval for long‑tail and noisy queries.
problem_solved: How to train semantic text embeddings for large‑scale, multi‑category e‑commerce search so they generalize to long‑tail/noisy queries while capturing graded relevance and remaining compatible with production and policy constraints.
method: Mine: automatically extract large‑scale weak positives and negatives across categories using scalable heuristics (e.g., logs, co‑purchase, catalog signals) to form initial contrastive pairs.
Refine: apply a graded contrastive training stage that re‑weights and uses curated hard negatives to separate exact matches, acceptable substitutes/complements, and non‑relevant items.
Production focus: design supervision and training that respect product/policy constraints and enable efficient embedding inference for retrieval at scale.
impact: Provides practitioners a scalable recipe to produce embeddings that better recover relevant and substitute products for noisy, long‑tail queries and integrate cleanly into production retrieval systems, improving overall search quality and robustness.

paper_title: Mine and Refine: Optimizing Graded Relevance in E-commerce Search Retrieval
paper_authors: Jiaqi Xi, Raghav Saboo, Luming Chen, Martin Wang, Sudeep Das
